Interactive D3 treemap

pv_treemap.Rd

A hierarchy as nested rectangles: each cell's area encodes its value, its hue names its top-level branch, and deeper levels fade a step toward the background. Cells are labelled where the label honestly fits; hovering a cell dims the other branches and shows the full path and share of the total.

Usage

pv_treemap(
  data,
  levels,
  value,
  labels = "auto",
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  mode = "auto",
  duration = 550,
  source = NULL,
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  elementId = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame in long form: one row per leaf.

levels

Character vector of column names, outermost grouping first, defining the hierarchy. The first level takes the palette colours, so it allows at most 8 distinct groups.

value

Name of the numeric column summed within each cell. Values must be non-negative — a cell's size is an area.

labels

Write names inside the cells? "auto" (the default) labels exactly the cells the text honestly fits into; TRUE squeezes labels into cells with about 20% less room than that (the text must still fit at all — tiny slivers stay blank); FALSE draws no cell text, leaving the names to the tooltip alone.

title, subtitle

Optional chart heading text.

mode

"auto" (default: follow the viewer's light/dark setting), "light", or "dark".

duration

Entrance transition length in ms.

source

Optional source/credit line, shown small and grey at the bottom left — e.g. "Source: Bundesamt für Statistik".

width, height, elementId

Standard htmlwidgets sizing arguments.

Value

An htmlwidget.

Examples

luzern <- pv_city_landuse[pv_city_landuse$city == "Luzern", ]
pv_treemap(luzern, levels = c("group", "category"), value = "hectares",
           title = "Land use in the city of Lucerne")
